title: Slowed and Reverb Maker – Free Online Tool
description: Free online slowed and reverb maker. Upload an audio file, adjust speed, pitch and reverb live in your browser, and export MP3 or WAV. No signup, no watermark.
heroText: Turn any song on your device into a slowed and reverb version in about a minute. This free tool loads your audio in the browser, plays the effect live as you adjust speed, pitch, reverb and bass, then renders the finished track for download. No signup, no watermark, and your file never leaves your device.

hero.alt: A producer working late at night in a dim bedroom studio, reaching toward a glowing laptop
hero.caption: Late-night sessions are where most slowed edits are born — one laptop, one track, no studio.

sections.title: The console, deck by deck
sections.body: Three decks sit on this screen: load a track, shape it, then render the file. All of it runs in the browser, so the sliders keep responding while the song plays.

items.title: Deck 1: load a track
items.body: Drag an MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG, FLAC or AAC file onto the drop zone, or press Choose file. The file decodes on your device and its waveform appears in the second deck. Try the sample loads a short built-in tone if you want to test the controls before committing a song.

items.title: Deck 2: shape it live
items.body: Three presets set the numbers for you: Classic Slowed + Reverb (0.80x, -2 semitones, 55% reverb, +4 dB bass), Daycore (0.75x, -5, 40%, +4 dB) and Nightcore (1.25x, +4, 12%, 0 dB). Or drag speed anywhere from 0.5x to 1.5x, pitch across 12 semitones each way, reverb from 0% to 100% and bass from 0 to 12 dB yourself. Play preview follows every change once a track is loaded, and the trim fields keep only the seconds you choose.

items.title: Deck 3: render and download
items.body: Pick WAV for a lossless 16-bit file or MP3 at 192 kbps for a smaller one, then press Render. The summary names the source file, its length and the finished length, and Download saves the file to your device. With no track loaded, Render says Load an audio file first instead of producing an empty file.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Three steps, all inside this page. Nothing is uploaded, because every audio operation runs in your browser through [Web Audio](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Audio_API), the open web standard for real-time sound.

steps.title: Load your audio file
steps.body: Drop in an MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG, FLAC or AAC file from your device, or press Choose file. The browser's own decoder turns it into an audio buffer in memory and draws the waveform, so a typical three-minute song is ready in a couple of seconds.

steps.title: Slow it down and shape the sound
steps.body: Apply Classic Slowed + Reverb, or set speed and pitch yourself. The speed control plays the track slower tape-style, so the pitch falls with it — 0.80x lands about four semitones down on its own — and the pitch field adds whole semitones on top of that drop. Reverb runs through a decaying room impulse, bass through a low-shelf boost at 120 Hz. Trim start and trim end cut the file to the section you want before any of that applies.

steps.title: Export the finished track
steps.body: Render runs the same audio graph offline, so the downloaded file is the version you previewed, plus the reverb tail (up to 1.6 seconds when reverb is on). The summary shows the source length and the rendered length before you download WAV or MP3.

sections.title: Formats and file handling
sections.body: Inputs are MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG, FLAC and AAC, which is what phones and laptops already produce. Exports are WAV at 16-bit or MP3 at 192 kbps. [The slowed and reverb guide](/how-to-make-slowed-and-reverb/) has the starting settings for each control.

items.title: WAV when quality matters
items.body: The WAV export is uncompressed 16-bit PCM at your browser's audio sample rate, so it opens cleanly in an editor or a video timeline and loses nothing in a second pass.

items.title: MP3 when it has to travel
items.body: MP3 is encoded at 192 kbps, which keeps a slowed track small enough to send, upload or drop into a video editor without a noticeable loss on phone speakers.

items.title: Your file stays on your device
items.body: There is no upload endpoint: the audio lives in browser memory until you close the tab. That is also why the tool needs no account, no quota and no watermark.

faq.question: Is this slowed and reverb maker really free?
faq.answer: Yes. Loading a file, all three presets, every slider, the trim fields, and both WAV and MP3 export are free, with no account, no quota and no watermark. The processing runs on your own device, so there is nothing for us to meter or charge.

faq.question: What settings make the classic slowed and reverb sound?
faq.answer: The Classic Slowed + Reverb preset applies 0.80x speed, -2 semitones of pitch, 55% reverb and +4 dB of bass boost. Press the preset, then adjust any slider by ear: most edits sit between 0.75x and 0.85x speed, with reverb strong enough to hear the tail on the last snare.

faq.question: Do I need to install anything or sign up?
faq.answer: No. The tool is a page in your browser on phone or desktop, with nothing to install and no sign-up step. Open it, load a file and start adjusting; closing the tab discards the audio from memory.

faq.question: Which file formats can I use?
faq.answer: Load MP3, WAV, M4A, OGG, FLAC or AAC from your device. Export as WAV (16-bit, uncompressed) for editors or MP3 at 192 kbps for sharing. The rendered file follows the settings you just previewed, including trim start and trim end.

faq.question: Can I speed a song up instead of slowing it down?
faq.answer: Yes. Raise speed and pitch and the same console produces a nightcore-style sped-up version; the Nightcore preset does it in one press at 1.25x and +4 semitones. The [nightcore maker page](/nightcore-maker/) opens with that preset already applied.

faq.question: Can I publish the result on social media?
faq.answer: That is your call, not ours. Slowing down a commercial recording creates a derivative of it, so if you publish the result you are responsible for having the rights you need. This site grants no copyright clearance and never receives your file.
